name: join_many_to_many_link
comment: A many-to-many joins twice: the link (alias l0) is NOT projected and hangs off the root; the target (j0) hangs off the link via 'parent' and is projected. Join order is declaration order.

sqlite.sql: select t.id as t_id, t.name as t_name, t.email as t_email, t.display_name as t_display_name, t.created_at as t_created_at, t.updated_at as t_updated_at, j0.id as j0_id, j0.role_name as j0_role_name, j0.created_at as j0_created_at, j0.updated_at as j0_updated_at from users t left join user_roles l0 on l0.user_id = t.id left join roles j0 on j0.id = l0.role_id

sqlserver.sql: select t.[id] as [t_id], t.[name] as [t_name], t.[email] as [t_email], t.[display_name] as [t_display_name], t.[created_at] as [t_created_at], t.[updated_at] as [t_updated_at], j0.[id] as [j0_id], j0.[role_name] as [j0_role_name], j0.[created_at] as [j0_created_at], j0.[updated_at] as [j0_updated_at] from [users] t left join [user_roles] l0 on l0.[user_id] = t.[id] left join [roles] j0 on j0.[id] = l0.[role_id]

postgres.sql: select t."id" as "t_id", t."name" as "t_name", t."email" as "t_email", t."display_name" as "t_display_name", t."created_at" as "t_created_at", t."updated_at" as "t_updated_at", j0."id" as "j0_id", j0."role_name" as "j0_role_name", j0."created_at" as "j0_created_at", j0."updated_at" as "j0_updated_at" from "users" t left join "user_roles" l0 on l0."user_id" = t."id" left join "roles" j0 on j0."id" = l0."role_id"
